question.problem:
Write the following expression as a single logarithm.

$4\operatorname{log}⁡t+4\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{2})+4\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{3})=4\operatorname{log}⁡(${{field-1}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the product rule for logarithms:

$$
{log}_{n}⁡a+{log}_{n}⁡b={log}_{n}⁡(ab)
$$

If we factor the given expression and use the product rule for logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4\operatorname{log}⁡t+4\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{2})+4\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{3}) & =4(\operatorname{log}⁡t+\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{2})+\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{3})) \\  & =4\operatorname{log}⁡(t\cdot {t}^{2}\cdot {t}^{3}) \\  & =4\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{1+2+3}) \\  & =4\operatorname{log}⁡({t}^{6}).\end{aligned}
$$
